newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australian prime minister starts Indonesian visit.
newsitem.headline: Australian prime minister starts Indonesian visit.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard met President Suharto on Monday at the start of his first official visit to Indonesia since taking office six months ago.
He drove straight from Jakarta's Sukarno-Hatta international airport to meet the Indonesian leader at Freedom Palace, where he was greeted by an artillery salute booming out across the city.
While relations between the two neighbours have been at times rocky, Howard's visit is seen as boosting ties and emphasising his government's commitment to Asia.
Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Tim Fischer said in Jakarta last week Howard's visit was a "reflection of the dynamic relationship between Australia and Indonesia".
It was also about "further building the economic linkage" between the two countries, Fischer added.
Indonesia is Australia's 12th largest trading partner and one of its fastest growing markets.
Following his initial meeting with Suharto, Howard was laying a wreath at the Kalibata national heroes' cemetery and later attending a state banquet hosted by the Indonesian leader.
He will have further talks with Suharto on Tuesday and leaves for Japan early on Wednesday. His two-nation visit had earlier been postponed after his wife fell ill.
